verses.1: My spirit is pleased with three things; these are approved in the sight of God and men:
verses.2: the harmony of brothers, and the love of neighbors, and a husband and wife agreeing well together.
verses.3: My soul hates three kinds of things; and I am greatly distressed over their souls:
verses.4: an arrogant pauper, a wealthy liar, a foolish and senseless elder.
verses.5: The things that you have not obtained in your youth, how will you find them in your old age?
verses.6: How beautiful it is for a grey head to have judgment, and for elders to know counsel!
verses.7: How beautiful it is for those who are aged to have wisdom, and for those who are honored to have understanding and counsel!
verses.8: Great experience is the crown of the aged, and the fear of God is their glory.
verses.9: I have magnified nine things, overlooked by the heart; and a tenth, I will declare to men with my tongue:
verses.10: a man who finds joy in his children, and one who lives to see the undoing of his enemies.
verses.11: Blessed is he who lives with a wise wife, and he who has not slipped with his tongue, and he who has not served those unworthy of himself.
verses.12: Blessed is he who finds a true friend, and he who describes justice to an attentive ear.
verses.13: How great is he who finds wisdom and knowledge! But there is no one above him who fears the Lord.
verses.14: The fear of God has set itself above all things.
verses.15: Blessed is the man to whom it has been given to have the fear of God. He who holds to it, to whom can he be compared?
verses.16: The fear of God is the beginning of his love; and the beginning of faith has been joined closely to the same.
verses.17: The sadness of the heart is every wound. And the wickedness of a wife is every malice.
verses.18: And a man will choose any wound, but the wound of the heart,
verses.19: and any wickedness, but the wickedness of a wife,
verses.20: and any obstacle, but the obstacle of those who hate him,
verses.21: and any vindication, but the vindication of his enemies.
verses.22: There is no head worse than the head of a serpent,
verses.23: and there is no anger above the anger of a wife. It would be more agreeable to abide with a lion or a dragon, than to live with a wicked wife.
verses.24: A wicked wife changes her face. And she darkens her countenance like a bear. And she displays it like sackcloth. In the midst of her neighbors,
verses.25: her husband groans, and hearing of this, he sighs a little.
verses.26: All malice is brief compared to the malice of a wife. Let the fate of sinners fall upon her!
verses.27: As climbing over sand is to the feet of the aged, so is a talkative wife to a quiet man.
verses.28: You should not favor a woman’s beauty, and you should not desire a wife for her beauty.
verses.29: The anger and disrespect and shame from a wife can be great.
verses.30: The wife, if she has primacy, is set against her husband.
verses.31: A wicked wife debases the heart, and saddens the face, and wounds the heart.
verses.32: A wife who does not make her husband happy enfeebles the hands and weakens the knees.
verses.33: The beginning of sin came from a woman; and through her, we all die.
verses.34: You should not provide an exit to your water, not even a little; nor should you give permission for a wicked wife to exceed the limit.
verses.35: If she will not walk at your hand, she will confound you in the sight of your enemies.
verses.36: Tear her away from your body, lest she abuse you continually. [ Sirach 26 ]
